Teuvo Teravainen's career has come full circle: a Stanley Cup in Chicago as a young player, 555 games in Carolina, and now a second stint with the Blackhawks. Sixteen games into this season, he is fighting for a lineup spot. Mark Lazerus of The Athletic reported on Nov. 12 that Teravainen would come out of the lineup if Patrick Kane returned, and trade speculation has already started connecting him with Carolina again.

The numbers explain why. He has 2 goals and 8 points, but only 11 shots, and his expected goals, the quality of his chances, add up to just 1.06. He has no goals in his last ten games. At five-on-five, Chicago has had about 42% of the chance quality with him on the ice, roughly what the team manages without him, which says the problem is bigger than one winger.

There is some bad company in that. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, but also noted he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league and was better than his goals. Still, a playmaker needs the puck in dangerous places, and right now it isn't getting there.
headline: Teuvo Teravainen is running out of room in Chicago
